entries.claim: Exactly 4 of the 583 post-mechanism findings that carry a falsifier have `falsifier_verdict == ERROR` together with `verified: True` and no second instrument (0.6861%), so the defect is the label rather than the decision, and the guard is a ratchet that tolerates those 4 by name while failing on anything new.
entries.why: The evidence file `/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/tests/test_errored_falsifiers_are_not_read_as_verification_2026-09-10.py` reads real archives rather than describing them: re-executing its own `_runs()` and `_misreads()` helpers returns denominator 583 across 17 post-mechanism runs, population 4 (exp42 C0032, exp42 C0046, exp55 C0003, exp55 C0010), rate 0.6861063464837049 — the entry's figure to 4 decimal places, so the quoted number travels with executable code even though the test pins the denominator only as `> 400`. The ratchet is not vacuous: patching `_runs` in memory to yield one synthetic ERROR+verified record takes both guard tests red ("an ERRORed falsifier is being read as verification in a run not on the known list" and "5 cases against the 4 recorded; the ratchet has slipped"). The four proportionality claims are executed, not asserted in prose — all 4 carry `escalated: True`, exactly 1 reached CLOSED, and exp47 C0055 is excluded because it genuinely carries `bugzilla_attempted: True, bugzilla_verified: True`, which I confirmed is the only record in the whole archive set excluded by that clause (5 ERROR+verified total, 1 removed). One adjunct class asserts on `reference_runner_v3.py` source text, but it is about the runner's message wording — a text property — and is not the entry's central claim. 7 tests pass.
entries.residual_work: The entry names none. One latent weakness not named by the entry: `_misreads()` excludes on the PRESENCE of any key starting with `bugzilla`, not on its value, so a future record carrying `bugzilla_verified: False` would escape the ratchet silently; today no such record exists.

entries.claim: The founder's premise is refuted for DeepSeek specifically — `tools = None` is a documented 2026-06-06 mitigation with a working compensator, and DeepSeek supplies runnable falsifiers more often than the pooled other seats (103 of 468, 22.01%, Fisher p = 0.0106) — so the real defect was the compensator failing silently at 3 endings, now all announced.
entries.why: Every quoted figure reproduces exactly from the committed script it names: `/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/scripts/deepseek_falsifier_supply_2026-09-09.py` prints DeepSeek 103/468 = 0.2201 Wilson [18.5%, 26.0%], 325/1925 pooled, Fisher p = 0.0106155, odds ratio 1.3893, statsmodels CI [1.082945841492411, 1.7821950205067114]. The three silent endings are driven by execution, not grep: a raising stub client hits the dispatch-failure path and must print "FAILED to dispatch" plus the 402, a client returning prose with no fence must print "no runnable block", and a good repair must print "format-repair applied" and replace the text — all three log lines exist at `bench/decomposed_dispatch.py:356,360,369`. Two guards stop the suite passing for the wrong reason: `test_the_fixture_actually_needs_repair` proves `NEEDS_REPAIR` matches `_FINDING_PRESENT_RE` and not `_RUNNABLE_FALSIFIER_RE`, and `test_a_response_needing_no_repair_never_dispatches` asserts zero paid dispatches on the common path. Only the caller's own except clause is checked by source text, narrowly justified in-file because the surrounding function performs a paid dispatch; I confirmed the replacement is live at `bench/experiment_11_orchestrator.py:1528-1557`, where the bare `except Exception: pass` is gone and `FORMAT-REPAIR DID NOT RUN: ... treat this reply's falsifier supply as UNCOMPENSATED` is emitted. 6 tests pass.
entries.residual_work: The entry itself flags that absolute falsifier-supply rates run 12% to 35% across every seat and that this "is a larger question than this item asked", and that Gemini is tool-enabled and higher still at 25.54% (script confirms 119/466). Not named by the entry: the founder's literal instruction ("fix DeepSeek and test it") was refused on evidence rather than parked in `experimental_notes/PARKED_FOR_THE_FOUNDER.md` the way task 2.2's comparable replay-invalidating refusals were, so the refusal has no founder ruling on file.

entries.claim: A sweep of the 3 frozen exp56 arm configs against 210 runner modules found 18 off-switches of which 9 are read by the runner (50.0000%), 12 carry a documented reason and 6 carry none, and nothing was changed.
entries.why: The instrument is real and its two named self-inflicted bugs are genuinely guarded — `/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/tests/test_capabilities_disabled_by_config_2026-09-10.py` asserts the scan covers >100 modules including `launcher_core.py` and excludes `tests/`, and pins the `ENABLEMENT`/`ALLOWANCE` patterns by positive and negative example (`enable_tools` matches, `verbose` does not). 13 tests pass. But the entry's headline figures no longer come out of the script it names. Running `scripts/capabilities_disabled_by_config_2026-09-10.py` at HEAD prints "of 15 off-switches found, 6 are READ by the runner = 40.0000%", Wilson [19.8245%, 64.2532%], Clopper-Pearson [16.3364%, 67.7130%] — not 18, 9, 50.0000%, Wilson [29.0310%, 70.9690%], and so not 12 of 18 documented either. The cause is that `sk_enabled` was flipped to true in all 3 arms at 2026-09-10 17:58 BST on founder instruction, 18 minutes after the entry's own last correction stamp of 17:40 BST, removing 3 rows from the population. Two consequences sit uncorrected in the entry: it quotes `_sk_note` verbatim as "S_k off in all three arms. The admissibility gate has never rejected anything — 0 of 3816...", whereas the file now opens "S_k ON in all three arms. TURNED ON 2026-09-10 17:58 BST on the founder's explicit instruction"; and "NOTHING WAS CHANGED, deliberately" is false of these configs as of that flip, which the evidence test itself records but the entry does not. Separately, the entry's stated surviving finding — the 6 unexplained switches, `hardened_gate_enabled` x3 and `_ouroboros.max_papers_per_round` x3 — is printed by the script but pinned by no assertion in the test, which asserts only that `merge_arbitration_enabled` and `immune_memory_enabled` are read by nobody; the residue can therefore drift without going red. The evidence file's own module docstring is likewise stale against its bodies, still saying sk_enabled is false in all 3 arms and naming 6 unread fields where the script now reports 9.
entries.residual_work: The entry names `hardened_gate_enabled` (read by the runner, no recorded reason, all 3 arms) and `_ouroboros.max_papers_per_round = 0` (read by nobody, no recorded reason, all 3 arms) as "the residue worth a decision", filed as A18. It also says whether `sk_enabled` should be false is the founder's call — since overtaken by his 2026-09-10 instruction to turn it on, which the entry has not absorbed.

entries.claim: The falsifier intake parser can now be studied by a run — per-reply telemetry records labels seen against blocks recovered, wired and cleared per run — and the first measurement reverses the "parser drops findings" impression at 132 of 138 fenced labels = 95.6522%.
entries.why: The mechanism half is established by execution, not description. bench/tests/test_intake_parser_is_studied_2026-09-10.py calls falsifier_intake_telemetry directly: a fenced label is recovered, a bare label counts as seen-but-not-fenced, both rates are emitted, and an empty fenced denominator yields None rather than 0.0. I verified the wiring independently rather than trusting the test: _note_intake immediately precedes every parse_findings call site in the active v3 runner (reference_runner_v3.py:8484-8485, 8733-8734, 8777-8778, 8802-8803, 8839-8840), _INTAKE_TALLY.clear() fires at the run entry point (:12427), and the tally is emitted into result["intake_parser"] at :15299. The figure half does not hold. The entry says 132 of 138 = 95.6522%, Wilson [90.8392%, 97.9924%]; its own named evidence file's docstring says 132 of 140 = 94.2857%, Wilson [89.1297%, 97.0764%] — the same measurement with two different denominators, and only one can be right. The entry's is the inconsistent one: it also states 411 raw labels and 271 carrying no fence, and 411 - 271 = 140, not 138. No committed script produces either figure — grep for falsifier_intake_telemetry across the tree returns only bench/runner_core.py, bench/reference_runner_v3.py and the test itself, and the test asserts a band (lo_f > 0.85, hi_r < lo_f), not the quoted rate. Re-running the archive scan today reproduces neither pair (119 replies gives 357 raw / 189 fenced / 180 recovered). The qualitative reversal is genuinely established by the band assertion against the live archive; the specific rate quoted to the founder is not. Two tests also assert on source text for behavioural properties — test_the_tally_is_cleared_per_run checks '"_INTAKE_TALLY.clear()" in src' and test_every_parse_site_is_covered compares string counts within one file — though test_it_accumulates does execute the tally, so the property is not left wholly ungrepped.
entries.residual_work: None stated by the entry. Outstanding by audit: reconcile 138 against the evidence file's 140 and correct whichever is wrong, and commit the script that produces the raw and fenced rates so the figure travels with its producer rather than living as prose in the entry and a second, differing number in the test docstring.

entries.claim: A run now detects the one-model-wearing-several-labels condition and refuses study item 46 rather than reporting a cross-architecture correlation it lacked the architectures to measure, with a control proving the refusal is conditional rather than hardcoded.
entries.why: The detector reads seat LABELS, not architectures, so it cannot fire on the condition the entry names. study_programme_report computes models = {e.get("source_model")} and sets answerable = len(models) > 1 (bench/reference_runner_v3.py:844, :879). source_model is assigned model_id at registration (:1954), and model_id is mc.label (bench/runner_core.py:221) — the seat's label string. So a panel of six seats all resolving to one model, each wearing its own label, yields six distinct strings and answerable: true. I proved this by execution twice, not by reading. Against a real archived registry (bench/logs/exp55_v3_control_20260823T153955Z/runner_state.json) the function returns answerable: true with distinct_source_models [CC2, ChatGPT, Codex, DeepSeek, Gemini]. Then against an explicitly simulated panel — labels CC2-SIM, Gemini-SIM, ChatGPT-SIM, DeepSeek-SIM, Codex-SIM — run_is_simulated(cfg) returns True while study_programme_report returns answerable: true, why_not: null, and names five "distinct_source_models". The refusal fires only when every seat shares one literal label, which is a narrower and different condition from the one the entry describes. This is decisive rather than theoretical because the correct signal is already in hand and ignored: the call site passes cfg (reference_runner_v3.py:15321), run_is_simulated(cfg) lives in the same module (:6949) and keys on the mandatory -SIM suffix, and grepping the function body for "cfg" matches only the signature line — the parameter is accepted and never read. The named evidence cannot catch this: test_the_cross_architecture_item_refuses_on_one_model builds a fixture where both entries carry source_model "CC2", i.e. one label, and the control test_it_becomes_answerable_with_distinct_models feeds three labels (CC2, Gemini, DeepSeek) which in a simulated run would be one model. Both tests pass and both test labels where the claim is about architectures. The entry's sentence "a future run cannot report a cross-architecture correlation it did not have the architectures to measure" is falsified by the runs above.
entries.residual_work: The entry states its own limit honestly — "DONE as far as it can go without you ... fixing it needs genuinely distinct architectures, which means paid dispatch — your category, not mine" — and that part is a fair deferral. What the entry does NOT flag, and what this audit adds, is that the detection it claims to have built does not detect the stated condition: gate answerable on run_is_simulated(cfg) (already passed in, already available) and/or on a resolved-model field rather than on seat labels, and add a test that feeds -SIM labels and requires answerable: false. Until then the entry should not be marked DONE.

entries.claim: The note vagueness linter never counts the founder's quoted words and so can never gate his input, while a paraphrase of him remains linted — proven by execution against a sentence engineered to trip the two rules the linter enforces hardest.
entries.why: The evidence establishes the claim and the boundary on both sides. bench/tests/test_founder_words_never_gate_2026-09-10.py executes the real linter (loaded from scripts/note_vagueness_lint.py) against TRIPPING, a sentence carrying a spelled number and an unnamed subject. The negative control comes first and is what makes the rest mean anything: the identical sentence in the assistant's own prose fires on BOTH rules, so the exemptions are a boundary and not a vacuous pass. Inline double-quoted: 0 counted. Inside a verbatim region: 0 counted and at least 2 still REPORTED, so nothing is hidden while nothing is gated. Four real rulings of his, quoted from the record, all count 0. A paraphrase ("The founder wants ...") is still caught, which the test argues is the rule rather than a loophole. The end-to-end case — a note consisting only of his quoted words — counts 0. Nine tests, matching the entry's stated count, and all pass today. I checked the one place the claim could still have failed, since the test measures lint() + verbatim_paragraphs() rather than the production partition(): hooks/pre-commit runs the linter CLI and extracts the count with grep -oE '^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+ finding' | tail -1, which matches only the final total line, and that total is len(counted) from partition() (scripts/note_vagueness_lint.py:569, :583). The per-file ratchet therefore reads exactly the number the test measures as zero, so the claim holds end to end.
entries.residual_work: None stated by the entry, and none material found. Two hairline gaps worth noting without changing the verdict: the test helper reimplements the counted/exempt split instead of calling partition(), the function the CLI and hook actually use — immaterial only because verbatim_paragraphs() delegates to region_state() and partition's two structural additions (future stamp, unbalanced region) are not sentence-level rules that a quotation could trip; and the end-to-end test never invokes hooks/pre-commit itself, so the link from lint count to commit refusal rests on reading the hook rather than on running it.

entries.claim: The quote exemption in scripts/note_vagueness_lint.py ran per sentence, so a quotation spanning a sentence boundary lost the exemption on every fragment but the last; moving the mask before the sentence split removed 8 false positives and added 0.
entries.why: The BEHAVIOURAL half is fully established and the guard can fail. bench/tests/test_note_vagueness_lint_2026-08-23.py passes 17 of 17; its 4-test class TestAQuotationSpanningSentencesStaysExempt CALLS LINT.lint on fixtures rather than asserting on source, and covers the defect case, the single-sentence comparator, a negative control (the same violation outside a quotation must still fire), and the masking regression the first fix caused. I mutation-tested it: copying scripts/note_vagueness_lint.py to a scratch file and making mask_quoted return flat unchanged makes the multi-sentence fixture report 'SPELLED NUMBER (Rule 27: use digits)' again, so the test is not vacuous. The fix is present at scripts/note_vagueness_lint.py:150 (mask_quoted) applied inside sentences() at :232. PARTIAL because the QUANTITATIVE half no longer reproduces from the script the entry cites. Running `python3 scripts/quote_exemption_effect_2026-09-09.py` today prints 407 notes scanned, 987 findings before, 29 removed, 19 ADDED, 2.94%, Wilson [2.1%, 4.2%] -- against the entry's '379 notes ... 8 false positives removed, 0 added, 0.70% of 1138 findings, Wilson [0.4%, 1.4%]' -- and it EXITS 1, because its last line is `return 1 if added else 0`, i.e. its own regression signal is now firing. I diagnosed the 19: they are not new findings. count() keys on (paragraph index, kind, text); comparing on (kind, text) alone over experimental_notes/Bugzilla_Verbatim_Compendium_2026-08-21.md gives 0 removed and 0 added, so the 19 are the same findings renumbered by the paragraphs() unification recorded at scripts/note_vagueness_lint.py:177. Substance intact, cited numbers stale, and the entry's discriminating claim '0 added' is contradicted by its own committed script.
entries.residual_work: The entry itself names none -- it reads as closed. Outstanding in fact: refresh the 5 quoted figures from a re-run, and make quote_exemption_effect_2026-09-09.py's added-count index-insensitive (compare on kind and text) so its non-zero exit stops being a standing false alarm on a fix that introduced nothing.

entries.claim: The panel brief format is the standard for the full paid 6-model panel by construction, because bench/confer_maths_panel_2026-09-05.py validates the brief and refuses a non-conforming one before any seat is paid.
entries.why: bench/tests/test_panel_brief_format_2026-09-09.py passes 29 of 29 and the load-bearing test EXECUTES the dispatcher: test_the_dispatcher_REFUSES_a_bad_brief_before_paying_a_seat runs confer_maths_panel_2026-09-05.py as a subprocess with PANEL_ONLY=__none__ and asserts returncode 2, 'REFUSED' in stderr, and 'paid' in stderr. I confirmed the wiring independently: main() at bench/confer_maths_panel_2026-09-05.py:419 calls _validate_brief_or_refuse() as its second statement, before the paid-seat list is even built at :423, and the function's own docstring records that main() is the only path to a paid seat. The bypass is real and announces itself (:406-408), the refusal names the format file (:414) and the bypass variable (:415). The validator is shown to discriminate rather than reject uniformly (test_the_validator_is_not_merely_hostile measures across archived BRIEF.md files and requires min < max), and the template passes its own rule. Two qualifications that do not overturn the claim. First, the entry double-quotes *"3 of the 5 seats are PAID; a defective brief costs money and returns nothing usable"* as 'the refusal message'; that string is a SPLICE and no artefact emits it -- the first clause is the stderr line at :410-411 ('3 of the 5 seats are paid:'), the second is prose at bench/directives/universal/panel_brief_template.md:5. Under the quote-convention (double quotes mean verbatim) that is a fabricated verbatim. Second, 'there is no second route a paid review could take' is over-stated at repository scope: bench/ holds roughly 58 other confer_* dispatchers, many wired to openrouter, none calling the validator. The paid claim still survives, because the only OTHER generic brief-driven panel dispatcher, bench/confer_panel_2026-08-28.py, is free-seats-only (MODELS = cc2, fable, both claude_cli at :62) -- but that same script bypasses the validator entirely, so the entry's 'the same code path serves the free and paid panels' is false for the standalone free panel.
entries.residual_work: None stated by the entry. Suggested: repair the spliced verbatim quotation, and either narrow 'no second route' to the maths-panel dispatcher or wire the validator into bench/confer_panel_2026-08-28.py so the free-panel half of the sentence becomes true.

entries.claim: The Zenodo token-rotation instructions the founder asked for on 2026-08-19 were delivered on 2026-09-10 as 2 documents with 5 steps, the 2 scopes and a confirmation command, backed by a checker that confirms the rotation and never prints the token.
